- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–15% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5.0), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 10–20% downward correction if sentiment drops or stabilizes.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 5–10% for low sentiment with upward momentum.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean-reversion events; if 3–5 consecutive days show price convergence, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overbought bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early days (1–5) when sentiment is volatile; apply a 5–10% downward adjustment for first 5 days if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- If sentiment history shows a sharp transition from negative to positive, model often misses the reversal; increase forecast by 5–10% in the first 3–5 days of sentiment shift.
